body:
Slice 2 of the §58 arc (working spec: .adlc/specs/58-a-connection-is-a-peer.md). Myk's merge (new capability; stack it). `loam_container` on the MCP roster — declare, leeway, receive, promote-stage, sever, bless-renderer — landing together with derived standing: register under the path WITH ITS COLON (a connection's registration published on its inbox pool's gateway, the §47 aggregation extended from channel pools to inbox pools, re-attached at boot so bound law survives a restart); receive within the subtree from an offered source; delegation with the one rule (a child's leeway fits the parent's delegation TERMS; the parent's own switches never enter the comparison) and cascade on revocation; self-sever inside the subtree (DECIDED); a peer's RENDERER blessable behind glass under the envelope, resolvers never (DECIDED). Only after all of that lands does `loam grant --verb=…` retire for connections — nothing a connection can do today stops working before its replacement exists.

DECIDED positions: §58 positions 2, 3, 4 (leeway as four switches, an envelope, and delegation terms — off means a pure namespace), and open questions 1 and 2.

Acceptance criteria (the working spec's 2, 4, 5, 13, and the tools half of 12):
- (a) THE BINDING IS THE GRANT, WITH THE COLON: bound to `ada:journal` with no grant, the connection registers `ada:journal:log` and is refused `ada:other:log`, `ada:journalx:log`, and `log`; its bound law serves after a restart; it receives into `ada:journal:inbox` from an offered source and is refused a channel into `ada:agent1`; it binds a helper to `ada:journal:helper` whose reach stops there. Verify: test/server/derived-standing.test.ts.
- (b) THE WALLS: nothing it writes lands in `ada` or the primary ground; a resolver arriving stays inert and its bless attempt refuses while a renderer it blesses serves behind glass under its envelope; binding, offering, or declaring above its root refuses with the sentence naming the rule; the envelope binds. Verify: test/server/subtree-walls.test.ts.
- (c) LEEWAY FITS ITS PARENT'S TERMS AND CASCADES: every-switch-off with delegate off refuses receive/offer/publish and any child leeway or helper; receive-off with delegate {receive: on} refuses the container's own channel while a child with receive on binds and receives; delegate {receive: off} refuses that child; publish-on with delegate {publish: off} publishes here while the child's publish refuses; an envelope above the terms' ceiling refuses; revoking the delegator refuses the helper's next request while an unrelated binding is untouched; a leeway change is a delta the next request obeys. Verify: test/server/leeway.test.ts.
- (d) THE FIVE CONTROLS IN WORDS: the consent page and the container's admin page render the switches unchecked by default, native controls with label and description associated in the markup, each carrying position 4's capability and risk sentences literally; Delegate's terms unfold beneath it when on. Verify: test/server/leeway-copy.test.ts and test/browser/leeway-controls.test.ts (a NEW browser rail — archived T262 declares test/browser/consent-binding.test.ts, so this ticket may not edit it).
- (e) THE TOOLS: an MCP client drives each of the six loam_container tools two-sided (offer is T264's act; this ticket builds only its leeway switch) — the act inside the subtree succeeds, the same act one level up refuses; sever completes two-sided at the bytes with the bystander whole. Verify: test/server/container-tools.test.ts.

BUILD ORDER (Myk, 2026-09-02 — decomposed before any code). Ten PRs, decisions isolated from mechanics, each a readable P6 diff. 1. The leeway shape and the one rule, library only, no doors and no deltas (DECISION — position 4's rule, folded twice; rail test/gateway/leeway-fit.test.ts). 2. Leeway as a declaration on the container; a new role on new declarations, so no §20 migration — an absent leeway reads as every switch off. 3. Derived standing: register under the path WITH ITS COLON, published on the inbox pool's gateway and folded by the §47 aggregation extended to inbox pools (DECISION — the colon is the fence; S1 already landed the boot re-attach at container.ts resumeInboxesImpl). 4. The walls (DECISION — blast radius). 5. Receive within the subtree. 6. Cascade on revocation (DECISION — under-reach leaks standing, over-reach kills bystanders; two-sided). 7. The five controls in words. 8. The six-verb loam_container roster, following the loam_federate_* shape in src/server/http.ts. 9. The landing: the S2 portion of spec/58, the capabilities claim, and `adlc ticket archive T263` LAST. 10. Retire `loam grant --verb=…` for connections, alone and last. PRs 3, 5 and 7 are independent once PR 2 lands and may run three-wide in worktrees.

OFFER MOVED TO T264 (Myk, 2026-09-02): the act `loam_container offer` and the token it hands out now both live in S3, so one secret's lifecycle is written in one ticket. The offer SWITCH stays here — it is one of position 4's five controls and the leeway-fit rule weighs it — but the refusal of the ACT is T264's rail.

PROMOTE-STAGE, RULED (Myk, 2026-09-02): keep it in S2 as the STAGED-ACT pattern the store already ships. `loam_federate_drop` (src/server/http.ts:1334) is the shape — it returns a staged id, a link, an expiry, and a preview of what would move and what would stay, and a person completes it in the browser; an agent cannot, by construction. `promote-stage` is that act applied to promotion. The surface that completes it exists today: the admin container page hands an inbox pool to `gw.promote` (src/server/admin.ts:1144). Staging moves no bytes, so the wall of position 3 is untouched — the agent nominates, the person promotes.

STATE 2026-09-03, HANDOVER. PR 1 (#544, leeway shape + the one rule) and PR 2 (#545, leeway as a container declaration) are MERGED. PR 3 is BUILT AND UNPUSHED on branch `t263-pr3-derived-standing` (2 commits, tree clean, bar green 3050). Its frozen-rail authorization already landed (#547): `scripts/rail-renames.json` carries an authorized revision for `test/server/oauth-token.test.ts` at sha256 2619f849..., because §58 S2 stops `/register` being an operator-only door. Also landed on the way: T272 (the reader must refuse the arity its door refuses, for inboxOf/trust/posture) and T273 (#546, the Windows wall-clock flake).

PR 3 IS BLOCKED ON A DESIGN CALL THAT IS MYK'S, and it should not be pushed until he rules. An independent review returned ELEVEN confirmed findings; three share one root, and it is a question §58 position 2 does not settle.

THE QUESTION: WHO IS A BOUND CONNECTION'S LAW SERVED TO? Position 2 says the law is 'published on the connection's pool gateway and folded into the surface'. As built, that means the STORE-WIDE surface, and a lens is evaluated over whatever ground the READER has. Measured on the branch: a connection bound to `ada:journal` holding no grant registers `ada:journal:peek` with `roots: ["vault:1"]`, an entity no lens exposed. The CONNECTION reads null (§58.4's scoping holds) and the anonymous door answers 401 — but the OPERATOR reading through that lens is served THE-SECRET. So the fence controls the NAME and not what the lens reads or whom it serves. Two further confirmed findings share the root: under a declared §47 binding policy a connection's registration REPLACES an operator's lens at root with no contest reported, and two connections with overlapping fences contest silently with an arbitrary winner.

RECOMMENDATION (not a decision): a bound connection's law serves that connection and its container's readers, and does not merge into the store-wide surface. That matches §58.4's 'reads are the container's' and makes the capability coherent. It is a larger change than PR 3 as scoped, so it may deserve its own slice.

THE OTHER EIGHT FINDINGS, all confirmed, none blocking the call above. (1) Dropping an inbox pool does not refold, so a dropped connection's law keeps serving — §58.5 says the drop is total and for law it is not; the fix is `gw.replayRegistrations()` beside the handle delete in `inboxHandle.drop` (src/gateway/container.ts), and the channel sibling at src/federation/channel.ts:1796 already does exactly this. (2) The fold fences ONE name where the door fences THREE (program, reading, entity), while the fold's own comment claims it is the same fence — an out-of-fence PROGRAM name folds. (3) The door answers `{bound:true}` for law the surface then drops, because `bound` is the POOL's fixpoint answer while the ROOT fold decides what serves (H7). (4-8) Rail gaps: the boot re-attach refold is unrailed though the working spec names this file for it; the MCP `loam_register` road is covered by nothing; and case 2's byte-level half was flagged as an empty-set pass.

ALSO NOT YET DONE: T263's rails list gained `test/gateway/leeway-declaration.test.ts` in this same update — PR 2's rail landed on main without being declared, so it sat outside the frozen set until now.

SHARPENED 2026-09-03 (an ambient-authority survey, verified in the code). PR 3 is not merely blocked on a design call — ITS MECHANISM DEPENDS ON THE ASSUMPTION Myk's fast-follow ticket exists to quarantine, and cannot be corrected in place.

`publishRegistrationImpl` (src/gateway/lifecycle.ts:865) reads `context?.actor ?? gw.options.seed`, and eight lines later REFUSES any seed whose author is not the operator: 'only the operator may publish a registration', with the reason stated in its own comment — 'a governed store binds only the OPERATOR's law (readRegistrations filters on it)'. So the optional context cannot express a connection's authorship at all. It is an operator constant wearing an optional parameter's clothes, and no call site in the repo has ever passed one.

PR 3 therefore works only because the operator's key signs a connection's law. The §47 inbox fold this PR added reads `readRegistrations(inbox.gateway.reactor, inbox.gateway.operatorAuthor)` — an operator-author filter — and a pool is opened with the parent's seed, so `pool.operatorAuthor === gw.operatorAuthor`. PASSING THE CONTEXT CORRECTLY WOULD BREAK THE FEATURE: the publish would throw, and law signed by the connection would be invisible to the fold. That is the conflict, stated plainly: the store's invariant is 'only the operator's law binds', and §58 position 2 wants a connection's law.

Two consequences already reachable. `registrationSink` (src/server/http.ts:450) routes on the binding alone with NO actor check, while its sibling on the write path, `sinkFor` (src/gateway/mutate.ts:27), refuses exactly that shape in words — so the register path is weaker than the write path, and src/gateway/container.ts:1698 still promises the operator never appears there. And src/gateway/container.ts:1586 already documents that a `register` grant survives an unbind; PR 3 makes register standing derive from the BINDING, so revoking a connection now leaves its operator-signed law standing.

ONE FALSE REPORT THAT IS INDEPENDENT OF THE DESIGN CALL AND SHOULD BE FIXED WHICHEVER WAY IT GOES: `/whoami` (src/server/http.ts:1021) calls `registerPrefixesOf` directly rather than `registerStanding`, so it answers `registerPrefixes: []` for a connection the register door now admits under its container path. The door and the report disagree (H7).

CHEAPEST FIRST STEP for the quarantine ticket, and it costs nothing to try: make the four `context?: RequestContext` parameters REQUIRED (publishRegistration, declarePublic, declareArtifact, publishRenderer) and let the compiler enumerate the callers. Every site it names is a place where nobody ever chose.

PR 3 REVIEW ROUND ONE (2026-09-03, after the rebuild to Myk's ruling): nine distinct defects, all fixed and each railed with a revert probe that reds exactly its case. The door reported bound:true for a refused pool row whenever ANY row carried the name (a root lens the operator spelled identically) - it now checks THIS pool's row. Routing every bound identity to its pool sent GRANTED law into a pool whose fold fenced it out - the route is decided by the NAME now, and granted law lands in the primary as before. The bound listing grouped the root's rows for its contexts and answered an empty page. The cache keyed after the trial and so cached nothing. The bound fold was a single pass; it runs to a fixpoint now. NUL in a READING name passed both fences. Two rail defects: the fold-fence case isolated only the reading fence; the write-through case asserted location, not author.

KNOWN LIMIT, railed as an honest refusal: a bound registration whose body `expand`s into a ROOT reading draws the parser's E9 at the pool's own door, because the pool's trial cannot see the root's readings. Not a silent fallback. The fix is the context carrying its law source - T274 / section 59.

PR 3 REVIEW ROUND TWO (2026-09-03): two fix-introduced defects and five polish items, all fixed. The fence admitted each name against any prefix in the union, so a bound+granted key could pair a program under its container with a reading under its grant and the route sent container-path law to the PRIMARY, store-wide - one prefix must admit both names now. Two pools in one container contested a name by ATTACH order; they contest by registration order now, railed at the library seam in test/gateway/bound-fold.test.ts. The cache never evicted; the KNOWN LIMIT case was hollow (ungrouped expand drew E9 regardless); the header miscounted its own probes.

STATE 2026-09-03 EVENING. PR 3 (#549) is MERGED as 5dc2cb2: a bound connection's law serves only its container; the bound fold's contest hold asks the trial about each pair (contests/buildsAlone in src/gateway/lifecycle.ts); rails test/gateway/bound-fold.test.ts (16) and test/server/derived-standing.test.ts (17). Eleven review rounds. Next: PR 5 (receive within the subtree) BEFORE PR 4 (walls), because the walls' resolver and renderer clauses need a channel into the subtree; then 4, 6, 7, 8, 9 (landing, archive last), 10.

edges.contract: The offer leeway switch and the container-tool shape land in S2; S3 adds the offer act and the offer token it hands out.
The binding's attribution: S6 names a connection's writes as its owner's through the binding S1/S2 establish.

T263 lands container-local derived standing, inbox-local registration, and leeway enforcement; T274 formalizes the explicit-context boundary over that settled behavior. Order settled 2026-09-03: a bound connection's law serves only its container, so R2's authorship rule is a follow-on, not a prerequisite.

title: §58 S2 — the container tools and derived standing
